name: Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia 93 (SPG93)

criteria.description: Progressive spasticity and weakness of the lower limbs
Biallelic pathogenic variants in ABHD16A gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
Intellectual disability or global developmental delay

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Progressive lower-limb spasticity and biallelic ABHD16A pathogenic variants are required. Intellectual disability and/or dysarthria support the diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by genetic testing. Clinical features may overlap with other complex HSPs.

imaging: Brain MRI: may show mild cerebral or cerebellar atrophy
other: Abnormal neurophysiology: spastic paraparesis on EMG

distinguishingFeatures: SPG11 often presents with thin corpus callosum on MRI
SPG11 may have more prominent cognitive decline and peripheral neuropathy
SPG15 may show retinal degeneration and thin corpus callosum
SPG15 may have more severe intellectual disability
SPG7 may present with optic atrophy
SPG7 often has later onset and less cognitive involvement

redFlags: Early-onset progressive lower-limb spasticity with cognitive impairment
Family history of autosomal recessive inheritance
references: Boutry M, et al. ABHD16A deficiency causes a complex hereditary spastic paraplegia by disrupting the phosphatidylserine cycle. Brain. 2019;142(6):1586-1604.
GeneReviews: Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia Overview (last update 2023)
commonPitfalls: Misattributing cognitive impairment to unrelated causes, missing the diagnosis of complex HSP
Assuming all hereditary spastic paraplegias lack intellectual disability
Failure to perform genetic testing for ABHD16A in complex HSP cases
Confusing with cerebral palsy in early-onset cases

extendedDiscriminators.feature: Absence of thin corpus callosum and more prominent cognitive impairment in SPG11
SPG93 has earlier onset and more frequent intellectual disability
Progressive course and family history suggest SPG93 over static cerebral palsy

ruleOutCriteria: Absence of biallelic pathogenic ABHD16A variants
Presence of alternative genetic diagnosis explaining symptoms
